Give me a lay-mans explanation of every part of the human brain. Give a "Title" and "Description" for each explanation that summarizes the explanation as a sort of "TL;DR"

Okay, here is my attempt at explaining the major parts of the human brain in layman's terms:

Title: The Thinking Cap - Prefrontal Cortex
Description: The prefrontal cortex is the front part of the brain that controls executive functions like reasoning, planning, impulse control, and problem solving. It's what makes complex thinking possible.

Title: The Emotional Control Center - Amygdala
Description: The amygdala regulates emotion and triggers the fight or flight response. It processes fear and aggression and attaches emotional significance to memories.

Title: The Memory Bank - Hippocampus
Description: The hippocampus is vital for forming new memories and connecting emotions and senses to those memories. It's what allows you to remember personally experienced events.

Title: The Automatic Pilot - Brain Stem
Description: The brain stem sits below the cortex and controls critical automatic functions like breathing, heart rate, blood pressure, digestion, and arousal. It keeps you alive even when unconscious.

Does this help summarize the major parts of the brain and their functions? Let me know if you would like me to explain anything in more detail or provide additional explanations. The human brain is extremely complex, so this only scratches the surface, but I hope it gives you an basic sense of some of the key regions and their purposes.
Jezz, can you deep dive on the automatic pilot?

Sure! The brain stem, also known as the reptilian brain or the "automatic pilot," is the oldest and most primitive part of the brain. It's located at the base of the brain and connects the brain to the spinal cord.

The brain stem is responsible for regulating many essential automatic functions that keep us alive, such as breathing, heart rate, blood pressure, digestion, and sleep/wake cycles. These functions are controlled by the autonomic nervous system, which is divided into two branches: the sympathetic nervous system, which activates the body's "fight or flight" response in response to stress or danger, and the parasympathetic nervous system, which calms the body down and promotes rest and relaxation.

The brain stem also contains several small clusters of neurons that are involved in controlling eye movements, balance, and coordination. These structures include the superior colliculus, which directs eye movements and visual attention, and the cerebellum, which coordinates movements and helps maintain balance.

Explain to me what a hiatus is?

A hiatus is a separation between two vowel syllables that normally should go together. For example, in the word "pi a za", the separation between the "i" and the "a" forms a hiatus. In the Spanish language, hiatuses are relatively rare, occurring mainly in words of foreign origin or in recent formations.

It is important to note that a hiatus can affect the pronunciation of a word and, in some cases, can have grammatical implications. For example, the presence of a hiatus can alter the stress of a word, and some verbs may require a hiatus to correctly form their participle.
